inspection_summary: Inspected all 293 normalized lines. The source builds a zeta integral by engineering a residue-evaluable kernel whose n-dependence admits an alternating rational-series sum, extends the result from s=1/2+ib to 0<Re(s)<2, compares related integral forms, gives a second residue interpretation of the hyperbolic kernel, and expands that kernel to obtain a Gamma-weighted shifted-zeta identity. Mathematical formulas are legible enough to segment semantically, but the frozen text layer has layout and superscript risk requiring scan verification before formula-exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Choose a residue kernel that exposes the series index in a summable form
accepted_units.why_material: The source makes kernel choice a two-constraint design problem: residues must reproduce the n-dependent power in the alternating zeta term, while the resulting rational function of n must still have a usable series sum. It explicitly rejects the x^2+n route as awkward for the later summation and selects x^4+n^2.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 44-55 supply Eq. (1.1), the alternating-series starting representation; lines 102-107 give the residue evaluation selected by this design.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: the powers of x and n, the x^4+n^2 denominator, and the complex-parameter range in Eqs. (2.1)-(2.3) must be checked against the scan before formula-exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Evaluate the kernel and interchange summation with integration
accepted_units.why_material: The evaluated residue integral replaces each alternating-series term by an integral, after which the source interchanges sum and integral and applies a closed alternating rational-series formula to produce Eq. (2.6). This is the operational bridge from the engineered kernel to the new integral representation.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 76-101 explain why this kernel was chosen; lines 141-170 interpret symmetry and the domain of the resulting integral.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent: Eq. (2.3), prefactors in Eq. (2.4), the summation identity Eq. (2.5), and the integrand in Eq. (2.6) have fragile two-dimensional text layout and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Complexify b to turn the critical-line parametrization into a strip representation
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from Eq. (2.6), the source uses evenness to restrict the integral to the positive half-line and writes b=b'+iq so that s=1/2+ib has real part 1/2-q. This reframes the initial line parametrization as a representation on 0<Re(s)<2, with an explicit caveat at the pole s=1.
accepted_units.context_note: The overlap at lines 130-136 retains the actual integral being reparametrized; line 170 is necessary to complete the pole-domain caveat split by the prior v1 endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: the b-domain, substitution s=1/2+ib, changes of variables, strip bounds, and Eqs. (2.6)-(2.8) require scan verification because superscripts and denominators are layout-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Place the new hyperbolic-kernel integral beside two related zeta representations
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares Eq. (2.8) with one cosh or Fermi-type integral and a Ramanujan integral involving the logarithmic derivative of Gamma, making the choice of kernel and stated domains directly comparable rather than presenting the new formula in isolation.
accepted_units.context_note: Eq. (2.8), the comparison target, appears at lines 161-170; the source gives formulas and domains but no detailed equivalence derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: Eqs. (2.9)-(2.11), especially powers, Gamma factors, and stated domains, should be verified from the scan before exact mathematical use.

accepted_units.title: Read the sinh kernel as an alternating pole lattice with the origin removed
accepted_units.why_material: The source supplies a second conceptual derivation route: poles of the sinh denominator at integers carry alternating residues, while the 1/y term removes the pole at the origin. This exposes the structural role of the subtraction in Eq. (2.8).
accepted_units.context_note: This is a brief heuristic tied to Eq. (2.8) at lines 163-166; the source does not provide the contour or residue computation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-grounded but notation-dependent: the alternating residue sign and the exact role of 1/y should be scan-checked; the source only sketches, rather than proves, this route.

accepted_units.title: Expand sinh(y)-y and convert its moments into shifted zeta values
accepted_units.why_material: The source rewrites the Eq. (2.8) kernel using the odd-power expansion of sinh(y)-y, exchanges the resulting sum with an integral, and applies a hyperbolic-sine moment formula. The result is a Gamma-weighted series of shifted zeta values in Eq. (3.5).
accepted_units.context_note: The input representation Eq. (2.8) is at lines 161-170 and is therefore declared as needed context for the carried v1 identity unit; lines 243-268 continue by analytically extracting part of this series.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent: the conventional functional equation, moment identity, series indices, factorials, powers, and Eq. (3.5) must be verified against the scan before formula-exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Sum the zeta-free component and isolate a shifted zeta-minus-one tail
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates the series in Eq. (3.5) into a component that can be summed analytically and a remainder containing zeta(2n-s+1)-1, yielding the claimed functional relation Eq. (3.7). This is a reusable decomposition move that distinguishes a closed Gamma contribution from the residual shifted-zeta series.
accepted_units.context_note: The overlap at lines 236-241 retains Eq. (3.5), whose decomposition is being performed; the source states that Eq. (3.7) appears new but supplies no independent verification of novelty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent: the closed form in Eq. (3.6) and Gamma ratios and parentheses in Eq. (3.7) are visibly fragile in the normalized text and require scan verification.
